analyses.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Team Collaborative Dialogue
analyses.research_question: Can fine-grained hierarchical dialogue-act annotation and context-aware sequence classification provide explainable measures of team communication and collaboration in long-running workplace Slack conversations?
analyses.methodology: The authors construct a hierarchical dialogue-act taxonomy containing 55 labels and use a reduced 18-label set for experiments on 4,035 sentences from six months of Slack communication by one eight-person software-development team. Annotation operates primarily at clause or fragment level, with speaker and timestamp context; the released experimental labels come from a single annotator after an earlier three-annotator agreement pass and guideline revision. They compare FastText with RoBERTa-plus-CRF sequential classifiers using one-, five-, and ten-utterance windows as well as time- and speaker-based segmentation, evaluating sentence-label accuracy. citeturn246367view0turn731643view4turn731643view5

key_findings.finding: The taxonomy explicitly distinguishes task assignment, voluntary task ownership, acceptance, requests, proposals, rejection, and counter-assignment, making it directly relevant to extracting action ownership and changes of responsibility from workplace chat. citeturn731643view2

Participant role and project responsibility can change the interpretation of an utterance from a request to an assignment, showing that owner assignment cannot always be inferred from surface wording alone. citeturn246367view0turn731643view4

The annotation scheme can separate multiple acts inside one sentence at clause or fragment granularity, but it also permits annotators to label larger multi-sentence blocks that are subsequently split automatically, so it is not a strict token-level evidence-span annotation scheme. citeturn246367view0turn731643view4

Longer conversational context improves dialogue-act classification relative to classifying isolated messages, with the best reported configuration using a ten-line window plus a one-hour temporal boundary and reaching 0.61 test accuracy versus 0.58 for the one-line setting. citeturn731643view5

Temporal proximity was a better contextual segmentation cue than restricting context to two speakers for this team, while the authors caution that the optimal segmentation strategy is probably team-dependent. citeturn731643view5turn731643view0

The study does not define a structured relation linking a deadline or temporal expression to a particular action, nor does it provide a dedicated representation for conditional obligations; negation is represented only indirectly through dialogue acts such as rejection and counter-assignment. citeturn731643view2

The proposed team metrics use sequences and response pairs such as question-answer and assignment-acknowledgment patterns, but the study has no independent endpoint measuring actual team performance. citeturn246367view0

limitations: The empirical corpus contains only one eight-person software-development team, one Slack channel, and six months of communication, limiting generalization to other organizations, industries, and communication platforms. citeturn731643view4

The final dataset labels are from a single annotator after an initial multi-annotator pass, and the paper states that full agreement results remained future work. citeturn246367view0turn731643view4

Slack threads and message reactions were not extracted, and annotators were not expected to consult project artifacts or transcripts from other days, potentially excluding context needed to resolve actions, owners, and decisions. citeturn731643view2
The authors lack an endpoint for actual team performance, so proposed collaboration metrics are not validated against project success or productivity outcomes. citeturn246367view0
The taxonomy does not explicitly encode deadline-to-action links, conditional obligations, normalized decisions, or provenance links from structured outputs back to exact token spans.
The authors note that tasks, efforts, roles, and capabilities require more sophisticated representations than those implemented in this initial work. citeturn731643view0
raw_claims: The study analyzes 4,035 sentences collected over six months from a single Slack channel used by eight researchers and programmers. citeturn731643view4
The full taxonomy contains 55 dialogue acts, while experiments use a reduced set of 18 labels. citeturn246367view0turn731643view4
Task assignment and voluntary task claiming are represented by distinct labels. citeturn731643view2
The taxonomy also distinguishes rejection with counter-assignment from ordinary rejection. citeturn731643view2
An utterance that resembles a request lexically can count as an assignment when the speaker's role gives it that function. citeturn731643view4
Annotators may label separate clauses or fragments within the same sentence with different dialogue acts. citeturn731643view4
Some longer text blocks receive one annotation before automatic sentence splitting, so annotation boundaries are not consistently exact textual evidence spans. citeturn731643view4
The paper models response patterns such as query-to-inform and assign-to-acknowledge transitions. citeturn246367view0
A ten-line time-segmented context window produced the highest reported test accuracy of 0.61. citeturn731643view5
The one-line classifier achieved 0.58 accuracy, indicating a measurable benefit from broader dialogue context. citeturn731643view5
The paper reports no independent measure of actual project or team performance against which the proposed communication metrics could be validated. citeturn246367view0
The implemented representation does not bind temporal deadlines to specific action records or formally encode conditional obligations.

analyses.title: Explicit, Implicit, and Scattered: Revisiting Event Extraction to Capture Complex Arguments
analyses.research_question: How should event argument extraction be reformulated and benchmarked when important event arguments may be implicit in context or distributed across multiple discontinuous parts of a discourse rather than appearing as one explicit span?
analyses.methodology: The authors create DiscourseEE from Reddit discussions about medications for opioid use disorder, selecting three event types and defining 41 argument roles across core, type-specific, subject-specific, and effect-specific categories. They annotate 396 post-comment pairs with 7,464 argument annotations using eight locally recruited annotators who received four weeks of training; at least two annotators produced arguments for each sample and a third reviewer resolved disagreements, yielding mean relaxed-match inter-annotator F1 of 0.811. Event argument extraction is reformulated as natural-text generation rather than span extraction, and extractive QA, generative FLAN-T5 models, and several zero-shot LLMs are benchmarked using relaxed-match and exact-match F1 measures on train/validation/test splits of 246/50/100 samples. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1turn945402view2

key_findings.finding: A majority of annotated event arguments require more than ordinary contiguous-span extraction: 51.2% are implicit and 17.4% are scattered, so 68.6% are either inferred or distributed across the discourse. citeturn326926view0turn568280view2

The paper demonstrates a fundamental limitation of exact evidence-span assumptions: implicit arguments have no directly stated source span, while scattered arguments are assembled from discontinuous information distributed through the document. citeturn568280view1turn945402view3
key_findings.section: 2 Event Extraction via Text Generation; 7 Related Work

key_findings.finding: Because the dataset stores generated natural-text argument values rather than start/end text spans, it supports semantic event reconstruction but does not itself provide strict provenance spans for every extracted argument. citeturn945402view0turn945402view2
key_findings.section: 2 Event Extraction via Text Generation; 5.2 Argument Extraction Models

key_findings.finding: Traditional extractive QA performs substantially worse on complex arguments, with mean relaxed-match F1 of 17.13 and recall of only 9.40% for implicit and 13.44% for scattered arguments. citeturn568280view2turn326926view3

Even the strongest evaluated generative system remains far from solving the task: GPT-4 with question-guided prompting reaches mean relaxed-match F1 of 41.98, while its best reported recall for implicit arguments is 36.53% and for scattered arguments is 54.12%. citeturn326926view3turn945402view3

Exact-match scoring can mark semantically correct generated arguments as wrong, and the authors' qualitative analysis indicates that exact-match evaluation therefore underestimates generative extraction quality. citeturn568280view4turn945402view3

The annotation process itself shows that scattered and implicit arguments create substantial human difficulty, including missed distributed evidence and the need for deeper contextual inference. citeturn326926view5

For the workplace-action research question, the paper contributes a useful representation of implicit and scattered arguments but does not study workplace communication or explicitly model action owners, deadline-to-action binding, conditional obligations, or negated obligations. Its ontology instead concerns health-advice events. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1

limitations: DiscourseEE is based on health-advice discourse from Reddit rather than workplace email or enterprise chat, so transfer to organizational action and decision extraction is untested. citeturn945402view0turn945402view1
Only 396 post-comment pairs were fully argument-annotated, although they contain 7,464 argument annotations. citeturn568280view5

Annotation is expensive and difficult to scale because annotators must generate argument values rather than select spans and because implicit and scattered arguments require substantial contextual reasoning. citeturn568280view5turn326926view5

Relaxed-match F1 depends on a manually selected semantic-similarity threshold, while exact-match F1 substantially underestimates semantically equivalent generations; the paper therefore lacks a fully satisfactory evaluation metric. citeturn945402view0turn568280view5
The benchmark assumes the ground-truth event type for the event-argument extraction experiments, simplifying the end-to-end extraction problem. citeturn945402view2

Models were evaluated with common zero-shot prompts rather than individually optimized prompts, so the reported LLM results are benchmarks rather than model-specific upper bounds. citeturn945402view2turn945402view3

Because the annotations are natural-text values rather than source offsets, the dataset is not directly suitable for applications requiring exact evidence-span provenance without an additional grounding layer. citeturn945402view2
The ontology does not contain explicit workplace constructs for owner assignment, deadlines attached to actions, conditional duties, or negated obligations.
